fixes.explanation: True, baker! The veil is made of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and finely spun linen, with cherubim skillfully worked into it (Exodus 36:35). The ten curtains got the same treatment (Exodus 36:8). Same fancy yarn, same cherubim. I once spent a whole afternoon getting one cookie to come out straight, and these folks are working cherubim into cloth.

A lion? Ooh, good guess, friend, but no. Bezalel makes two cherubim of hammered gold for the ends of the mercy seat (Exodus 37:7). Not a lion in sight. One cherub goes on one end and one on the other, all made from one piece of gold (Exodus 37:8).

You got it, baker! The cherubim have wings that spread upward, overshadowing the mercy seat, and they face each other, looking toward the mercy seat (Exodus 37:9). Two gold figures, wings up, facing each other. I can't even keep my eyes on one cookie.

problems.problem: It has 6 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.
Calling the cherubim angels adds an identification the passage does not make.
The joke about keeping a stamp lined up in a junk drawer does not make clear sense as a comparison to the craftsmen’s work.
Saying the baker showed confidence assumes something about the baker that their answer does not establish.
The text says the cherubim look toward the mercy seat, not that their eyes are on the same spot.
